result.topic_en: Worked examples of finding exponents x such that formulas like 2^x+1, 2^x-1, 2^x-3, 5^x-1 are divisible by a given prime, by successive reduction of residues, followed by the general problem of finding x with A K^x - a divisible by p.
result.transcription:
Fragmenta ex Adversariis depromta. 173
Exemplum II. Quaerere formulam $2^x+1$, quae divisorem habeat 29. Pro hoc divisore
potestates | residua | sive
$2^x$ | $-1$ | $-1+29=28=2^2.7$
$2^{x-2}$ | $7$ | $+36=2^2.9$
$2^{x-4}$ | $9$ | $-20=-2^2.5$
$2^{x-6}$ | $-5$ | $24=2^3.3$
$2^{x-9}$ | $3$ | $32=2^5.1$
$2^{x-14}$ | $1$ | $x=14$.
Exemplum III. Quaerere formulam $2^x+1$, quae divisorem habeat 73. Pro divisore 73
potestates | residua | sive
$2^x$ | $-1$ | $2^3.9$
$2^{x-3}$ | $+9$ | $-64=-2^6.1$
$2^{x-9}$ | $-1$ | $72=2^3.9$
$2^{x-12}$ | $9$ | $-64=-2^6.1$
$2^{x-18}$ | $-1$ |
unde apparet hanc quaestionem esse impossibilem.
Exemplum IV. Quaerere formulam $2^x-1$, quae habeat divisorem 23:
potestates | residua | sive
$2^x$ | $1$ | $24=2^3.3$
$2^{x-3}$ | $3$ | $-20=-2^2.5$
$2^{x-5}$ | $-5$ | $-28=-2^2.7$
$2^{x-7}$ | $-7$ | $16=2^4.1$
$2^{x-11}$ | $1$ | ergo $x=11$.
Exemplum V. Quaerere formam $2^x-3$, quae habeat divisorem 19:
potestates | residua | sive
$2^x$ | $3$ | $-16=-2^4.1$
$2^{x-4}$ | $-1$ | $-20=-2^2.5$
$2^{x-6}$ | $-5$ | $-24=-2^3.3$
$2^{x-9}$ | $-3$ | $16=2^4.1$
$2^{x-13}$ | $1$ | $x=13$.
Problema generalius. Invenire exponentem $x$, ut formula $AK^x-a$ datum habeat divisorem $=p$.
Solutio. Numerus ergo $AK^x$ residuum dare debet $=a$, cui aequivalet $a\pm\lambda p=K^\alpha b$, unde numerus $AK^{x-\alpha}$ residuum dare debet $b$, sive $b\pm\lambda p=K^\beta c$, sicque numerus $AK^{x-\alpha-\beta}$ producet numerum $c$, sicque hoc modo procedendo, donec perveniatur ad numerum $A$, quod quia nascitur ex $AK^0$, manifestum est esse debere
$x=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+$ etc.
Exemplum. Quaerere formulam $5^x-1$, quae divisorem habeat 17.
potestates | residua | sive | potestates | residua | sive
$5^x$ | $1$ | $35=5.7$ | $5^{x-5}$ | $-6$ | $-40=-5.8$
$5^{x-1}$ | $7$ | $-10=-5.2$ | $5^{x-6}$ | $-8$ | $-25=-5^2$
$5^{x-2}$ | $-2$ | $15=5.3$ | $5^{x-8}$ | $-1$ |
$5^{x-3}$ | $3$ | $20=5.4$ | $5^{x-16}$ | $1$ | $x=16$
$5^{x-4}$ | $4$ | $-30=-5.6$ | | |
Problema. Invenire exponentem $x$, ut formula $2^{2x}+2^x+1$ datum habeat divisorem $p$.

methods.what: Reduction algorithm: repeatedly add multiples of p to the residue to make it divisible by a power of the base, lowering the exponent, until residue equals A; x is the sum of the removed exponents
methods.quote: $a\pm\lambda p=K^\alpha b$, unde numerus $AK^{x-\alpha}$ residuum dare debet $b$
